edit.description: one guard over gate.run, shared by all three gate-run sites
the throwing-gate cases at both stages

summary: A gate that throws is recorded ok:false with the error's message, and the tick's verdict and merge bookkeeping complete as for a returned refusal
acceptance: A throw out of any gate reaches the tick as that gate's failure; the verdict is written and the merge is reverted or refused exactly as a returned ok:false would have it.
tests: a gate that throws is recorded as that gate's failure carrying the error's message
a tick whose gate throws writes its verdict instead of dying at the crash marker
an afterMerge gate that throws reverts the merge as a returned refusal would
notes: Three unguarded sites: src/Dispatcher.ts:2116 (fanout afterMerge), :2740 (wave afterMerge), :3729 (the span's gate loop). The guard is one helper the three share, not a try/catch pasted thrice (engineering.md, The fix lands at the mechanism); its home is build's call. The revert-refused catch at :2201 is the shape precedent.

edit.description: renderSweepWindow names the tip its frontier was drawn from
the cursor paragraph stamps the named tip
the named tip, populated and quiet

summary: The sweep window names the tip it was drawn from, so the closing tick stamps that tip instead of rediscovering a HEAD that moved
acceptance: Every rendered sweep window names one tip, and the prompt directs the closing tick to stamp exactly that rather than a sha it resolves itself.
tests: a rendered sweep window names the tip its frontier was drawn from
a sweep window with no commits past its cursor names the cursor as its tip
notes: renderSpecWindow:419 is the sibling line to match. The tip is the last of commitsPast(cursor) else the cursor — already read, so no second git call. plan-sweep.md:37 still says "the sha the frontier was derived from — never a HEAD that moved mid-rotation", which is the rule's retired wording.

edit.description: bound both render entry points, per the fail-open's own cite

summary: A window render refuses by name on any git failure, not only an unresolvable cursor — touchedPast's fail-open already promises that bound
acceptance: Every git failure inside a window render reaches the woken slice as the named refusal; nothing escapes promptArgs into an uncaught tick.
tests: a window render refuses by name when git fails for a reason other than an unresolvable cursor
notes: touchedPast (harness/windows.ts:783) wakes the slice on any git failure and names refusal as its bound; refusal is reached only from the !resolves leg of renderSpecWindow:391 and renderSweepWindow:497. A throw out of commitsPast/diffOf/retiredLines/bootstrap escapes phase.promptArgs — uncaught at src/Dispatcher.ts:1957 and :3281 — so the tick dies with no verdict. Carry the failure's own text into the refusal.

edit.description: the vitest factory over the api; the `prepare`/`worktreeRoot` options go
call the declared factory at load with the chain's own api
the factory type on the package surface
the schema's refusal of a non-factory runner
the factory called with the chain's api

summary: `runner` is declared `(api) => Runner` and called at chain load, so the vitest factory takes the engine's installer and the state root's worktree base from the API
acceptance: The declaration schema refuses a runner that is not a factory, naming the field; the chain factory calls the declared factory with its own FlumeApi; the vitest factory's base checkout is provisioned by that API's installer under the state root's worktree base, and no consumer constructs either by hand.
tests: a declaration whose runner is a Runner value rather than a factory is refused at load naming the field
the chain factory calls the declared runner factory with the same FlumeApi it received
the vitest runner factory places its base checkout under the state root's worktree base
the vitest runner factory provisions its base checkout with the installer from the API it was given
notes: Ruled in spec at 1d81a77. Breaking declaration-schema change with a chain-side twin: this repo's .flume/declaration.ts:63 still passes a vitestRunner({lanes}) value and .flume/ is outside build's fence, so chain load refuses every tick between this commit and the operator's edit -- an interactive session moves it the moment this lands. The package reaches the base as worktreesBase(api.paths.flumeDir) via ../src/paths.js; putting it on FlumeApi stays the parked question's call.

summary: The package's relocated-root refusal cites Committed-path discipline, the section that now states the precondition, and a test pins the refusal
acceptance: repoRelativeStateRoot's refusal cites the section stating the precondition, and a test holds the package to refusing a root outside the repository.
pins: the package refuses a state root resolved outside the repository, naming both roots
notes: harness/chain.ts:560 already refuses; it cites *Records as one file each*, which states no precondition. Nothing pins the refusal, so it is one deletion from being silently lost.
